source_text:
Κωφώθητε οὖν, ὅταν ὑμῖν χωρὶς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλῇ τις, τοῦ ἐκ γένους Δαυείδ, τοῦ ἐκ Μαρίας, ὃς ἀληθῶς ἐγεννήθη, ἔφαγέν τε καὶ ἔπιεν, ἀληθῶς ἐδιώχθη ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτον, ἀληθῶς ἐσταυρώθη καὶ ἀπέθανεν, βλεπόντων τῶν ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ ὑποχθονίων.
ὃς καὶ ἀληθῶς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ νεκρῶν. ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα ὃς καὶ ἡμᾶς τοὺς πιστεύοντας αὐτῷ οὕτως ἐγερεῖ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, οὗ χωρὶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ζῆν οὐκ ἔχομεν.
thought_title: The True Birth, Death, and Resurrection of Jesus
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Trallians against false teachers, and here he states the real events of Jesus's life as the ground of Christian faith.
pass_a_gloss: Be made deaf therefore, whenever anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ, the one from the family of David, the one from Mary, who truly was born, [and] ate and drank, truly was persecuted under Pontius Pilate, truly was crucified and died, while the heavenly and earthly and subterranean [beings] were watching. Who also truly was raised from the dead, his Father having raised him, according to the likeness [in] which also us, the ones believing in him, thus will raise his Father in Christ Jesus, apart from whom the true life we do not have.

choices.why: The aorist passive imperative has a permissive force: 'let yourselves be made deaf' or 'make yourselves deaf'; the passive form is kept to preserve the sense that this is a deliberate shutting of the ears.
The preposition χωρίς means 'without' or 'apart from'; 'apart from' preserves the spatial metaphor of separation from Christ as the criterion for rejecting speech.
The adverb is repeated four times in the source to emphasize the reality of each event against docetic denial; the repetition is kept in the literal gloss.

choices.term: βλεπόντων τῶν ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ ὑποχθονίων
choices.english: while the heavenly and earthly and subterranean [beings] were watching
choices.why: The genitive absolute construction marks attendant circumstance; the three adjectives are substantival and refer to beings in the three cosmic regions, so '[beings]' is supplied in brackets.
rejected: with heavenly, earthly, and subterranean beings looking on

choices.why: The phrase is awkward in the source; the literal gloss keeps 'according to the likeness' and marks the relative clause that follows as the point of comparison, preserving the source's syntax.
The articular infinitive ζῆν functions as a noun; 'the true life' captures the substantive use while keeping the adjective ἀληθινόν distinct from the adverb ἀληθῶς used earlier.

pass_b_english: So make yourselves deaf whenever anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ. He was of the family of David and of Mary. He truly was born, and he ate and drank. He truly was persecuted under Pontius Pilate, truly was crucified and died, while the heavenly, earthly, and subterranean beings were watching.
He also truly was raised from the dead. His Father raised him. According to this pattern, his Father will also raise us who believe in him, in Christ Jesus. Apart from him we do not have true life.

problems.quote: his Father having raised him. In the same way
problems.source_quote: ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα ὃς καὶ ἡμᾶς
problems.why: Missing 'according to the likeness/pattern' (κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα)
problems.fix: his Father having raised him. According to this pattern his Father will also raise us
problems.ruling: κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα ('according to the likeness') is omitted; meaning of the pattern/likeness is lost.

problems.why: ὁμοίωμα means 'likeness/pattern,' not 'same way'; ὃς καὶ = 'who also'
problems.fix: According to this likeness, who also
problems.ruling: ὁμοίωμα means 'likeness/pattern'; 'In the same way' loses this and merges with ὃς καὶ.

edits.old: his Father having raised him. In the same way his Father will also raise us who believe in him
edits.new: his Father having raised him. According to this pattern his Father will also raise us who believe in him

fixed: The omission and mistranslation both concern the same phrase; the edit addresses both by restoring 'According to this pattern' for κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα.

problems.quote: He truly was born, and he ate and drank. He truly was persecuted under Pontius Pilate
problems.why: Resembles 1 Timothy 3:16 or early creed but not exact Scripture citation; presented as fact.
problems.fix: Note as early confessional formula, not direct biblical quotation.

edits.old: He truly was born, and he ate and drank. He truly was persecuted under Pontius Pilate.
edits.new: He truly was born, and he ate and drank. He truly was persecuted under Pontius Pilate,

fixed: The reported problem is not real: the English already says exactly what the source says. The source presents these as facts about Jesus, not as a direct biblical quotation, and the English does the same.

last_rejected.quote: who was of the family of David and of Mary
last_rejected.source_quote: τοῦ ἐκ γένους Δαυείδ, τοῦ ἐκ Μαρίας
last_rejected.why: Uses 'family' instead of 'genus/race' sense; 'family' weakens the Davidic lineage claim.
last_rejected.fix: who was of the line of David and of Mary
last_rejected.ruling: γένος can mean family/descendants; 'family of David' is within normal range and not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: truly was persecuted under Pontius Pilate
last_rejected.why: ἐδιώχθη means 'was pursued/tried,' not 'persecuted'; legal trial before Pilate, not persecution.
last_rejected.fix: truly was brought to trial under Pontius Pilate
last_rejected.ruling: ἐδιώχθη commonly means 'persecuted'; 'under Pontius Pilate' is standard rendering of ἐπὶ with genitive.

polish.changed: Broke long sentences into shorter, clearer statements; made the subject of each clause explicit; clarified that 'his Father' refers to Christ's Father; removed awkward relative pronoun chains and translationese.

notes.why: 'Passible' (capable of suffering) vs 'passion' (suffering/death) are related but distinct; reader may miss Christological point.
notes.fix: Gloss 'passible' as 'capable of suffering' on first use.

polish.changed: Clarified the subject of each clause as Jesus Christ, smoothed the sentence flow, and kept all claims and qualifications exactly.

notes.why: Resembles 1 Timothy 3:16 or early creed but not exact Scripture citation; presented as fact.
notes.fix: Note as early confessional formula, not direct biblical quotation.
